Title: Hydration free energy of small molecules in water
Description: Estimates the free energy released when a small molecule is transferred from vacuum into water, a quantity that underpins how tightly a solvated ligand can be pulled into a binding site. Training used FreeSolv, the MoleculeNet set of 642 molecules pairing experimental hydration free energies with alchemical calculations. A graph transformer pretrained without labels on 10 million ChEMBL and ZINC15 molecules was fine-tuned on it, averaging three folds per prediction. FreeSolv is small and dominated by neutral organic compounds, so charged or unusual chemistry sits outside its range.
Interpretation: Hydration free energy in kcal/mol, where more negative values indicate stronger solvation.
